summary: pp.1-12: Pages 1-12 of PSEG Long Island's Performance Requirements for Large Loads Connected to the LIPA System (>= 20 MW threshold), covering scope, definitions, steady-state power factor and demand limits, active power ramp rate limits (20 MW/min), frequency ride-through, subsynchronous active power variation limits (Table 4-2), and the start of voltage ride-through requirements. | pp.13-24: Pages 13 through 24 of the PSEG Long Island / LIPA large-load performance requirements cover voltage and phase-angle ride-through, reactive current and overvoltage limits, power quality (flicker, rapid voltage changes, harmonics, radio frequency interference), and PSS/E and PSCAD simulation modeling obligations, with no checkable active-power ramp, step, or fluctuation-band limits. | pp.25-28: Pages 25-28 of the PSEG Long Island / LIPA large-load interconnection requirements cover EMT modeling obligations, facility modification notice procedures, performance and active power variation verification, power variation protection relay and ground source rules, and POI monitoring equipment (DFR, DDR, and power quality meter) specifications, with no explicit numeric active-power ramp, step, fluctuation, or dynamic-range limits.

constraints.snippet: The steady-state power factor of the Facility, determined by the average active power demand and the average reactive power demand over any 15-minute period shall be greater than 0.98.
constraints.notes: Steady-state power factor requirement in normal operation, evaluated over any 15-minute period.

constraints.snippet: Power demand shall not exceed 50% of Maximum Rated Demand or greater than 20 MW for longer than 0.10 seconds, occurring not more than once per day, unless authorized by PSEG Long Island Operations.
constraints.notes: Short-term exceedance allowance above Maximum Rated Demand at the POI; additional short-term limits are 10% for 1.0 second and 1% for 1.0 minute, each not more than once per day.

constraints.snippet: The Large Load Facility shall limit its active power demand as stated in the interconnection agreement during grid emergency conditions.
constraints.notes: Qualitative active power control obligation during grid emergency conditions.

constraints.snippet: The Facility’s maximum power ramp rate shall not exceed 20 MW/minute (measured as a change in active power over any 60 second period) for load increases or decreases under normal operating conditions, unless determined as necessary to meet other performance requirements specified.
constraints.notes: Applies to load increases or decreases under normal operating conditions when RMS voltage magnitude of all phases at POI > 0.9 pu for the 60 s period; applies individually and in aggregate for Demand-Synchronized Large Load Facilities. May be exceeded under emergency conditions as allowed in the Interconnection Agreement.

constraints.snippet: Frequency [Hz] | Minimum Ride-Through Time [sec]: > 61.8 May trip; > 61.2 299; <= 61.2 and >= 58.8 Continuous; < 58.8 299; < 57.0 May Trip.
constraints.notes: Frequency ride-through requirements; frequency measured over typically 50 to 100 ms.

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall not trip for an absolute rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) magnitude of less than 5.0 Hz/sec over an averaging window of at least 100 milliseconds.
constraints.notes: RoCoF ride-through requirement.

constraints.snippet: In the event of frequency at the POI increasing above 60.5 Hz, the Facility shall remain connected and operating at an active power no less than 70% of its pre-disturbance active power for a minimum of ten minutes. This requirement shall not apply if the frequency increases above 61.8 Hz for more than 100msec.
constraints.notes: Over-frequency response requirement.

constraints.snippet: In the event of frequency at the POI decreases below 59.5 Hz, active (real) power demand of the Facility shall be decreased by at least the lesser of 17% of the Rated Maximum Demand or 50% of the active power demand immediately prior to the frequency decreasing below the 59.5 Hz threshold. The reduction shall occur within 0.30 seconds of frequency decreasing and remaining below 59.5Hz, in accordance with PRC-006-NPCC-2 Attachment C.
constraints.notes: Under-frequency load shedding response; active power demand must remain at or below reduced levels until PSEG Long Island System Operations grants permission to increase.

constraints.snippet: In the continuous operating range (voltage at the POI between 0.9pu and 1.10pu; frequency between 58.8Hz and 61.2Hz), the Facility shall not cause amplification (negative damping) of active or reactive power oscillations in the subsynchronous frequency range defined as 0.1Hz – 55.0Hz.
constraints.notes: Qualitative small-signal subsynchronous oscillation damping requirement requiring frequency-domain transfer function assessment.

constraints.snippet: Facility Owner shall disclose the electrical characteristics of any processes creating cyclic variability of active power demand within a 10-minute period that exceeds more than 5% of Maximum Rated Demand.
constraints.notes: Disclosure threshold for cyclic variability processes rather than a hard operational limit.

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall not cause unstable behavior on the grid or materially degraded performance or operating life of other equipment connected directly or indirectly to the LIPA system, directly resulting from varying active power.
constraints.notes: Qualitative prohibition against adverse grid/equipment impacts from varying active power.

constraints.snippet: High Subsynchronous (5.0 – 55.0 Hz): The P0-pk,avg for the sum of any two adjacent frequency bins shall not exceed 3.5 MW0-pk,avg (10 second rolling window).
constraints.notes: Stated unit is MW0-pk,avg (zero-to-peak MW averaged over a 10-second rolling window). Per Section 4.5.3 (p. 10), FFT window is 1.0 s (1.0 Hz bins) at >= 600 Hz sample rate; verified over at least 600 s per normal operating mode. Applies individually and in aggregate for Demand-Synchronized Large Load Facilities.

constraints.snippet: Low Subsynchronous (0.1 – 5.0 Hz): The P0-pk,avg for the sum of any two adjacent frequency bins shall not exceed 10.0 MW0-pk,avg (60 second rolling window).
constraints.notes: Stated unit is MW0-pk,avg (zero-to-peak MW averaged over a 60-second rolling window). Per Section 4.5.3 (p. 10), FFT window is 10 s (0.10 Hz bins) at >= 60 Hz sample rate; verified over at least 600 s per normal operating mode. Applies individually and in aggregate for Demand-Synchronized Large Load Facilities. [CONFLICT: Conflicts with fluctuation_band_13 (p.12: 20.0 MW = 20 MW)]

constraints.snippet: Low Subsynchronous (0.1 – 5.0 Hz): The P0-pk,avg for the sum of all bins shall not exceed 20.0 MW0-pk,avg (60 second rolling window).
constraints.notes: Stated unit is MW0-pk,avg (zero-to-peak MW averaged over a 60-second rolling window). Per Section 4.5.3 (p. 10), FFT window is 10 s (0.10 Hz bins) at >= 60 Hz sample rate; verified over at least 600 s per normal operating mode. Applies individually and in aggregate for Demand-Synchronized Large Load Facilities. [CONFLICT: Conflicts with fluctuation_band_12 (p.12: 10.0 MW = 10 MW)]

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall ride through at least three distinct voltage deviation events (where the voltage between events re-enters the continuous operating range) within 10 seconds. The Facility shall not trip or change its power consumption by greater than 10% of maximum rated demand due solely to a certain number of voltage sags within a certain period of time.
constraints.notes: Voltage magnitude ride-through requirement for multiple consecutive voltage deviation events.

constraints.snippet: During voltages less than 0.9 per unit, the Facility may temporarily reduce the load consumption, but the load shall return to at least 90% pre-disturbance consumption from grid within one second of voltage recovery to 0.90 per unit. During this period of low voltage, the Facility’s active current shall not increase in response to a voltage decrease.
constraints.notes: Post-disturbance low-voltage ride-through load recovery obligation (return to >= 90% pre-disturbance consumption within 1 s of recovery to 0.90 p.u.) and prohibition on increasing active current during low voltage.

constraints.snippet: Table 5-1: RMS Low-Voltage Ride-Through Requirements | Voltage [p.u.] < 0.5: 0.15 sec; < 0.8: 0.5 sec; < 0.9: 2.0 sec.
constraints.notes: RMS low-voltage ride-through duration curve.

constraints.snippet: Table 5-2: RMS High-Voltage Ride-Through Requirements | V > 1.2: Refer to Cumulative Instantaneous High-Voltage Ride-Through Requirements; V > 1.1: 2.0 sec.
constraints.notes: RMS high-voltage ride-through requirement.

constraints.snippet: Table 5-3: Cumulative Instantaneous High-Voltage Ride-Through Requirements | V > 1.8: May Trip; V > 1.7: 0.0002 sec; V > 1.6: 0.001 sec; V > 1.4: 0.003 sec; V > 1.2: 0.015 sec.
constraints.notes: Cumulative instantaneous high-voltage ride-through thresholds and durations.

constraints.snippet: Facility shall be required to remain online for voltage phase angle disturbances at the POI in which the phase angle of the positive sequence fundamental frequency voltage waveform suddenly (within one 60Hz period) changes, or “jumps”, by up to 25 electrical degrees in either direction.
constraints.notes: Phase angle jump ride-through requirement within one 60 Hz cycle while voltage remains within 0.90 to 1.1 p.u. or ride-through envelope.

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall be required to remain online for any condition in the continuous range of voltage at the POI (0.9pu to 1.1pu) except where the negative sequence voltages exceed 2% of the nominal voltage for greater than 60 seconds or 5% for greater than 3 seconds.
constraints.notes: Negative sequence voltage ride-through requirement.

constraints.snippet: Reactive current demand of the Facility shall not exceed 50% of the current at Maximum Gross Demand for a period exceeding 10 seconds, or 100% of the current at Maximum Gross Demand for a period exceeding 1 second during and after voltage disturbances where the magnitude of any phase voltage at the POI is less than 0.9 times the nominal voltage.
constraints.notes: Transient reactive current demand limit during and after low-voltage disturbances (< 0.9 p.u.).

constraints.snippet: Sudden discontinuation of any amount of Facility apparent power demand shall not cause voltage at the POI to increase by more than 5% of the nominal voltage for longer than 1 second, or 20% of the nominal voltage for longer than 0.1 seconds.
constraints.notes: Load rejection overvoltage limitation at the POI.

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall not cause the root-mean-square magnitude of the POI phase-to-phase or phase-to-ground voltage, measured over a 1/60th second window, to exceed 1.2 p.u. of the nominal voltage, or to exceed 1.1 p.u. of the nominal voltage for a period exceeding 1.0 seconds.
constraints.notes: RMS temporary overvoltage limit; Section 5.6(a) also prohibits exceeding Table 5-3 cumulative instantaneous overvoltage limits.

constraints.snippet: Table 5-3 – Instantaneous Voltage Limits | 1.7 p.u.: 0.2 ms; 1.6 p.u.: 1.0 ms; 1.4 p.u.: 3.0 ms; 1.2 p.u.: 15.0 ms.
constraints.notes: Maximum cumulative duration of instantaneous overvoltage thresholds caused by the Facility.

constraints.snippet: Contributions of the Facility to Point of Interconnection voltage variations shall not exceed PST = 0.35 or PLT = 0.25 as defined in IEEE Std 1453.
constraints.notes: IEEE Std 1453 voltage flicker limits (Pst <= 0.35, Plt <= 0.25).

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall not cause Frequent Rapid Voltage Change, as defined in the latest version of IEEE Std 2800, at the Point of Interconnection greater than 0.025 times the nominal voltage.
constraints.notes: Frequent Rapid Voltage Change limit at the POI.

constraints.snippet: Abrupt change in POI RMS voltage magnitude and Rapid Voltage Change due to infrequent power transformer switching shall not exceed 10% of the nominal voltage for any duration exceeding one cycle of a 60 Hz period, shall not exceed 5% of the nominal voltage for greater than 0.1 seconds and shall not exceed 2.5% for 1.0 seconds.
constraints.notes: Voltage change limits for infrequent power transformer switching.

constraints.snippet: With the exception of infrequent energization of power transformers connected at or near the Point of Interconnection, Facility shall not cause abrupt changes to the root-mean-squared (rms) voltage magnitude at the POI greater than 2.5% of the nominal voltage and that occur at a rate of voltage change that exceed 0.025 times the nominal voltage per second, averaged over a one second period.
constraints.notes: Abrupt RMS voltage change (> 2.5%) and voltage rate-of-change (> 0.025 p.u./s over 1 s) restriction at the POI.

constraints.snippet: With the exception of restoration of operation following LIPA system faults, clearance from System Operations is required prior to any transformer energization producing a change in the rms magnitude of the POI voltage exceeding 2.5% of the nominal value for any duration exceeding one fundamental frequency cycle.
constraints.notes: Operational clearance requirement for transformer energization causing > 2.5% POI RMS voltage change.

constraints.snippet: Non-fundamental-frequency current components flowing between the Facility and the LIPA system at any given harmonic order, shall be less than the values specified in Table 6-1. Table 6-1 – Harmonic Current Limits | h < 11: 2.0%; 11 <= h: 1.0%; TRD: 3.0%.
constraints.notes: Harmonic current limits for facilities connected to strong systems (nominal SCR > 20 at POI), applicable above 120 Hz up to 3 kHz.

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall not cause an incremental increase in voltage distortion at any non-fundamental order from harmonic orders 2 to 4 or 6 to 50 by greater than 1% of the nominal voltage. The Facility shall not create an incremental fifth harmonic voltage component at the Point of Interconnection, exclusive of ambient distortion, greater than 0.3% of the nominal voltage.
constraints.notes: Incremental harmonic voltage distortion limits for facilities connected to weaker systems (nominal SCR <= 20 at POI), applicable above 120 Hz up to 3 kHz.

constraints.snippet: Table 6-2 – Harmonic Voltage Limits | 69 kV and below: Individual Harmonic 3.0%, THDv 5.0%; 138 kV: Individual Harmonic 1.5%, THDv 2.5%; 345 kV: Individual Harmonic 1.0%, THDv 1.5%.
constraints.notes: Total harmonic voltage distortion and individual harmonic limits at the POI for weaker systems (SCR <= 20).

constraints.snippet: The Facility shall not cause radio frequency noise to be radiated from any LIPA transmission line or substation that is of greater intensity than 200 uV/m measured at any point greater than 50’ beyond the perimeter of any substation, or 50’ from the centerline of any LIPA transmission line.
constraints.notes: Radio frequency interference limit measured per IEEE Std 430-1986 and ANSI C63.2-1996.

constraints.snippet: The facility-specific fast fluctuations in demand that are driven by the specific processes being performed by the large load are not required nor expected to be represented in the dynamic models. The fluctuations of demand must meet the requirements of this document and compliance will be demonstrated by other means described herein.
constraints.notes: Modeling requirement clarifying that fast process-driven demand fluctuations are validated outside dynamic models.

constraints.snippet: The Facility Owner shall provide a model representing the plant design, overall topology, major components, and a one-line diagram of the facility. The model shall be provided in Siemens PTI PSS/E format of the current version in use by NYISO.
constraints.notes: Steady-state positive-sequence fundamental-frequency model submission requirement.

constraints.snippet: The Facility owner shall provide a model, implemented in the Siemens PTI PSS/E dynamic simulation software, formatted for the PSSE version associated with the FERC 715 filing that NYISO is also using. ... The Facility owner shall provide an electromagnetic transients model, implemented in the PSCAD simulation software in the version currently in use by PSEG Long Island.
constraints.notes: Phasor domain dynamic (PSS/E, non-proprietary) and electromagnetic transient (PSCAD) simulation model submission requirements.

constraints.snippet: The EMT model shall be configured for the specific Facility. This model shall be provided to PSEG Long Island prior to the Resource being placed into commercial operation. The EMT model shall comply with NYISO Electromagnetic Transient (EMT) Modeling Guideline, UG 28.
constraints.notes: EMT model configuration, revision control, validation documentation, NDA availability, and NYISO UG 28 compliance requirements.

constraints.snippet: For any material change to the Facility, which is any change that could impact the performance of the facility with respect to these requirements, including but not limited to: changes in control parameters, firmware, or IT algorithms on any of the Major Facility Components, a detailed description of the proposed changes shall be submitted to PSEG Long Island – including updates to all affected simulation models as appropriate per Section 7 – at least 60 days prior to intended implementation at site.
constraints.notes: 60-day advance submission and approval requirement for material facility modifications.

constraints.snippet: Within 60 days of interconnection or within 60 days of a modification of the Facility per Section 8, the Facility owner shall provide verification of performance of the Facility to these requirements.
constraints.notes: Requires performance verification via field tests, lab tests, or detailed simulations, plus equipment/firmware/parameter documentation for AC-connected power-electronic Major Components.

constraints.snippet: Prior to interconnection, the Facility owner shall provide measurements or detailed simulation results of active power consumption that is representative of the Facility across the range of operating conditions that would be expected to occur for more than 600 consecutive seconds. The resulting active power variation data verifying compliance with the active power variation requirements shall be submitted to PSEG Long Island at least 60 days prior to implementation at site.
constraints.notes: Pre-interconnection active power variation verification data covering operating conditions lasting more than 600 consecutive seconds, due at least 60 days prior to site implementation.

constraints.snippet: A power variation monitoring relay shall be implemented to continuously monitor the active power at the POI and evaluate it against the limits in accordance with the Active Power Variation Limits section. If the limits are exceeded for a window period as defined in the Active Power Variation Limits section, then the relay shall initiate an immediate disconnection of the Facility from the system.
constraints.notes: Protection relay requirement for active power variation compliance; PSEG Long Island must be notified immediately if the relay is out of service.

constraints.snippet: The Large Load Facility shall not present a ground source to the LIPA transmission system unless otherwise stated in the Interconnection Agreement.
constraints.notes: Prohibits presenting a ground source to the LIPA transmission system unless specified in the IA; on-site generation is subject to generation interconnection requirements.

constraints.snippet: Data shall be retained for 90 days after a triggered event. Facility Owner shall provide recorded data to PSEG Long Island within 10 days on request. A digital fault recorder (DFR) shall record instantaneous voltage and current at the Point of Interconnection for a duration of 10 seconds when triggered. Data resolution shall be at least 128 samples per 60 Hz cycle.
constraints.source_section: Section 11. MONITORING / Section 11.1 Digital Fault Recorder
constraints.notes: Monitoring data retention/delivery and DFR recording duration and sampling resolution requirements at POI.

constraints.snippet: A dynamic data recorder (DDR) shall record active power, reactive power, and phasor magnitude and angle for voltage and current at the Point of Interconnection for a duration of at least 600 seconds when triggered. Data resolution shall be at least one sample per 60 Hz cycle.
constraints.notes: DDR recording requirements at POI; a DFR capable of capturing at least 600 seconds of event data may also serve as the DDR.

constraints.snippet: A power quality meter shall be provided that is capable of measuring and recording rapid and abrupt voltage change events, flicker, harmonic currents and harmonic voltages at the Point of Interconnection.
constraints.notes: Power quality monitoring capability requirement at the POI.
